title: Nourishing Argentinian Long-bean Empanadas
description: Resinous, tender, and festive, these empanadas feature long-beans, double-fried for an extra crispy texture, and are Shojin-friendly for a mindful meal.
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, salt, and black pepper. Add the cornmeal and stir to combine.
Add the vegetable shortening and use a pastry blender or your fingers to work it into the flour mixture until it resembles coarse crumbs.
Gradually add the water, stirring with a fork until the dough comes together in a ball.
Knead the dough on a floured surface for 5-7 minutes, until it becomes smooth and elastic.
Divide the dough into 12 equal pieces and roll each one into a ball.
Use a rolling pin to flatten each ball of dough into a thin circle, about 1/8 inch thick.
Place a tablespoon of the long-bean and chicken filling in the center of each dough circle.
Brush the edges of the dough with a little water and fold the dough over the filling, pressing the edges together with a fork to seal the empanada.
Heat a large skillet or frying pan over medium heat and brush with a little oil.
Cook the empanadas for 2-3 minutes on each side, until they are golden brown and crispy.
Note: Traditionally, empanadas are baked in a wood-fired oven, but you can also bake them in a conventional oven at 375°F (190°C) for 15-20 minutes, until golden brown.
You can also deep-fry the empanadas if you prefer a crisper exterior.
Note: For a Shojin-friendly version, use a vegetarian substitute for the chicken or omit it altogether.
If using chicken, ensure that it is organic and free-range for maximum nutrition.
Note: You can also use a food processor to quickly chop the long-beans and make the empanada dough.
Note: Traditionally, empanadas are served as a snack or dessert, but they can also be served as a main course or side dish.
Note: Empanadas are a great way to use up leftover vegetables and fillings, so feel free to get creative and experiment with different ingredients!
Ensure poultry is cooked to an internal temperature of 74°C / 165°F (juices run clear, no pink remaining) before serving.
